At WWDC 2021, Apple announced support for storing driver's licenses in Apple Wallet on iPhone. At the time, Apple marketed this feature as the final step to "completely break free from your physical wallet".

Here are the next batch of states where Apple Wallet driver's license support is coming…

Apple Wallet ID support

Five years after Apple first announced this feature, support has been gradually expanding across the United States. Currently, iPhone and Apple Watch users in 14 states and Puerto Rico can add a driver's license or state ID to Apple Wallet. You can see the full list here:

Where is this feature launching next? Here's what we know so far.

The following seven states have confirmed they are working on Apple Wallet driver's license support, have been listed by Apple as partners, or have previously appeared in Apple code:

  • Kentucky (launching "summer" 2026)
  • North Carolina (launching early 2027)
  • Oklahoma (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Utah (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Virginia (in the works, launch date TBD)
  • Connecticut (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)
  • Mississippi (status unclear, previously listed by Apple as a partner)

Meanwhile, the Secure Technology Alliance has been tracking the rollout of mobile driver's licenses across the United States. Here are the states that have begun exploring mobile ID support through legislation or studies, but have not been mentioned by Apple:

  • Indiana
  • Vermont
  • New Jersey
  • Florida
  • South Carolina
  • Tennessee
  • Missouri
  • Nevada
  • Wyoming

It's important to keep in mind that progress varies from state to state. A state merely exploring or developing digital ID support doesn't necessarily mean it will eventually launch, let alone support Apple Wallet.

Summary

As you can see, support for Apple Wallet driver's licenses remains a rather piecemeal rollout across the United States.

However, you don't have to wait for your state to support digital IDs in Apple Wallet to try out this feature.

Apple launched a new "Digital ID" feature last year, powered by your US passport. While it's not your driver's license, it lets you use your iPhone at TSA checkpoints in over 250 airports across the United States.

Have you stored an ID or driver's license in Apple Wallet on your iPhone? Have you actually used it? Let us know in the comments.
